conditions.name: Non-Specific Lower Back Pain
conditions.summary: Persistent lower back pain with no single identifiable structural cause. At MC Balans, we assess conventionally first, then look at structural, functional and regulatory patterns — combined with Traditional Chinese Medicine where appropriate — before recommending a plan.
conditions.recognition:
Non-specific lower back pain is pain in the lower back for which no single structural problem — like a fracture or a trapped nerve — fully explains what you're feeling. It's the most common type of lower back pain, and it can still be significant, frustrating and limiting, even without a specific diagnosis behind it.
You might recognize it as:
●	An ache, stiffness or sharp pain anywhere along the lower back — from a dull daily ache to pain that limits bending, sitting or standing for long periods
●	Pain that's affected by posture, movement, stress, or how tired you are
●	Stiffness, especially first thing in the morning or after sitting for a long time
●	Pain that hasn't fully resolved despite rest, painkillers, or previous treatment
If your pain radiates down your leg, follows an injury, or came on suddenly and severely, that may point to something more specific — see the section below on when to get it checked.
conditions.red_flags:
Before anything else, MC Balans checks that your complaint doesn't warrant immediate or specialist medical attention. Sudden severe pain with numbness, weakness or loss of bladder control needs urgent medical attention. Contact your GP or MC Balans promptly — before starting any TCM treatment — if you also notice:
●	Pain following a fall, accident or injury
●	Numbness, tingling or weakness spreading into your leg or foot
●	Unexplained weight loss, fever, or pain that is worse at night or at rest
●	A history of cancer, osteoporosis, or long-term steroid use
These signs can point to conditions such as a herniated disc, nerve compression, a fracture, infection or, rarely, something more serious — and they need conventional medical assessment first, not acupuncture. If none of this applies to you, your pain most likely falls into the non-specific category this page is about.
conditions.understanding:
Most lower back pain isn't caused by damage that shows up clearly on a scan. Instead, it's often the result of how your back is loaded, how it moves, how well it recovers, and how your nervous system is regulating pain signals — all of which can keep pain going even after any original trigger has healed. Where the pain is felt is often not where the problem starts or ends.
This is exactly why MC Balans doesn't stop at treating the symptom, but seeks to understand what is underlying the complaint.
conditions.approach:
Rather than treating a symptom in isolation, every assessment at MC Balans looks at your complaint through three connected lenses before any treatment is recommended:

Structure — how the physical parts of your body relate to one another: bones, muscles, fascia, scars, nerves, blood vessels, and circulation. Pain in one spot is often the result of tension, restriction, or compensation happening somewhere else in the chain. This lens looks at what's actually pulling on what, and why.

Function — how your body performs during ordinary daily life: walking, sitting, sleeping, working. Different systems in the body are meant to work together, and this lens identifies where that coordination is breaking down and affecting your movement or activity.

Regulation — how your body responds and adapts when something disrupts its normal functioning. This includes the influence of physical and emotional stress on your body's ability to regulate itself and recover, which can play a bigger role in persistent complaints than people expect.

Only once these three lenses point to a clear pattern does Dr. Lin or a member of the care team recommend a specific approach — acupuncture, herbal medicine, cupping, or another treatment — because it fits your case, not because it's the default response to your symptom.
conditions.assessment:
Your first visit is a consultation with Dr. Lin or Dr. Wang. Before you're called in, you'll fill out a short intake form covering your health history, insurance details, and the reason for your visit.

Intake
We start with your complaint, in your own words, and how it's developed — and check for any warning symptoms (see Red Flags).

Conventional medical assessment
We review your medical history and current medication, rule out the red-flag conditions above, and arrange further diagnostics or a referral if needed.

Structural assessment
We look at how the physical parts of your body — bones, muscles, fascia, scars, tissue, nerves, blood vessels, and circulation — relate to one another, and whether a change in one place is affecting another through tension, compensation, or restriction elsewhere.

Functional assessment
We look at how your body moves and functions in daily life, and how different regions work together — or don't — in ways connected to your complaint.

Regulatory assessment
We look at how your body responds and adapts when its normal functioning is disrupted — recovery, circulation, inflammation — and how physical or emotional stress may be affecting your ability to heal.

TCM assessment (where appropriate)
Where relevant, this includes a pulse and tongue examination as part of the TCM diagnostic model, offering a complementary perspective that can inform your treatment.

All of this comes together into one picture, and your treatment plan follows from it — built to address what's actually causing your complaint, not just the symptom.
conditions.expectations: Most patients notice some relief before their complaint is fully resolved, but resolving recurring issues usually takes more than one session — how many, and how quickly, varies from person to person and depends on what your assessment finds. Your practitioner will give you a clearer sense of what to expect once they've assessed you, and will adjust the plan as treatment progresses.
conditions.insurance: Consultations and treatments may be totally or partially covered depending on whether your insurance covers alternative/complementary care (aanvullende verzekering) — we can help you check this.
conditions.pricing: Assessment starts from €35 for a Western Medicine Consultation (under 20 minutes) or from €45 for a first TCM Consultation. Treatment pricing depends on what's recommended — for example, acupuncture is €70 per session and cupping is €10.

Functional assessment
We look at how your body moves and functions in daily life, and how different regions work together — or don't — in ways connected to your complaint.

Regulatory assessment
We look at how your body responds and adapts when its normal functioning is disrupted — recovery, circulation, inflammation — and how physical or emotional stress may be affecting your ability to heal.

TCM assessment (where appropriate)
Where relevant, this includes a pulse and tongue examination as part of the TCM diagnostic model, offering a complementary perspective that can inform your treatment.

All of this comes together into one picture, and your treatment plan follows from it — built to address what's actually causing your complaint, not just the symptom.

conditions.summary: Asthma can affect breathing and everyday activities. Complementary treatments may help support overall wellbeing alongside your existing medical care.
conditions.approach:
Rather than treating a symptom in isolation, every assessment at MC Balans looks at your complaint through three connected lenses before any treatment is recommended:

Structure — how the physical parts of your body relate to one another: bones, muscles, fascia, scars, nerves, blood vessels, and circulation. Pain in one spot is often the result of tension, restriction, or compensation happening somewhere else in the chain. This lens looks at what's actually pulling on what, and why.

Function — how your body performs during ordinary daily life: walking, sitting, sleeping, working. Different systems in the body are meant to work together, and this lens identifies where that coordination is breaking down and affecting your movement or activity.

treatments.name: Western Medicine Consultation
treatments.summary: A consultation with Dr. Lin to assess your symptoms, medical history and individual health needs, providing a medical perspective alongside MC Balans' broader approach to care and exclude life-threatening medical issues.
treatments.body: During a Western Medicine Consultation, Dr. Lin discuss your symptoms, medical history and current concerns to develop a clear understanding of your health situation. Where appropriate, the consultation may include a physical assessment and recommendations for further investigation, referral or treatment. The consultation can also help determine whether Western medical care, TCM, or a combination of approaches may be appropriate for your individual needs.

treatments.name: TCM Consultation
treatments.summary: A consultation focused on understanding why your body may not be functioning as it should, combining conventional medical assessment with an extensive analysis of the body's structural, functional and, where appropriate, Traditional Chinese Medicine balance.
treatments.body:
During a TCM Consultation, we look beyond the question of which disease you may have and instead explore what may be disrupting the way your body functions. This includes an assessment of structural and functional patterns and, where appropriate, the balance of the body from a Traditional Chinese Medicine perspective. The aim is to identify disruptions that may not always be visible through conventional diagnostics, but that may help explain persistent complaints or symptoms.
Safety always comes first. When there are indications of a condition requiring further medical diagnosis or treatment, we refer you back to your GP or medical specialist. Our broader functional approach can be particularly relevant for patients who continue to experience complaints despite normal test results or who feel that the underlying cause of their symptoms has not been fully understood.

treatments.name: Online Tongue Diagnosis
treatments.summary: With many complaints, you no longer have to leave your house with today's technology. Based on a photo of the tongue and answering a few simple questions, you too can have your personal herbal blend sent home.
treatments.body:
How does it work?

With many complaints, you no longer have to leave your house with today's technology. Based on a photo of the tongue and answering a few simple questions, you too can have your personal herbal blend sent home.

Step 1
You take three pictures of your tongue. You take the photos as close as possible so that the tongue is clear and sharp in the picture.

Step 2
Upload the photos in the form and fill out the questionnaire. Then press 'request' and follow the payment instructions.

Step 3
You will receive an email within 2 working days with a proposal for a personal herb mix.

Step 4
Click on the link in the email and follow the payment instructions to purchase the tea bags with herbs and have them delivered to your home.

Applications

treatments.name: Acupuncture
treatments.summary: A traditional Chinese medicine technique using fine needles placed at specific points on the body to relieve tension and restore balance.
treatments.body: Acupuncture is a well-established technique within Traditional Chinese Medicine, in which a trained practitioner places fine needles (size depending on the condition) at specific points on the body. Clinical evidence supports its use for a number of complaints, including certain types of pain and migraine. For other complaints, it is used within MC Balans' broader clinical model as a tool for addressing structural, functional and regulatory imbalance. At MC Balans, acupuncture is not a default response to a complaint — it's recommended once your assessment points to it being an appropriate part of your plan, often combined with other techniques to meet your specific needs.
treatments.aftercare: Each session is evaluated with the patient to track feeling, progress, and desire to continue the treatment. For certain conditions, follow-up examination sessions are recommended.

treatments.name: Acupotomy
treatments.summary: A specialized technique that combines acupuncture with a fine surgical needle to relieve chronic pain and release tension in muscles, tendons, and joints.
treatments.body: Acupotomy, also known as needle knife acupuncture, is a specialized technique that combines the principles of acupuncture with a fine surgical needle. Rather than a standard acupuncture needle, a slightly thicker needle with a small flattened tip is used to target areas of chronic tension, scar tissue, or adhesions beneath the skin. At MC Balans, this treatment is used to help relieve persistent pain and stiffness, particularly in cases where standard acupuncture has had limited effect. The doctor determines the size and placement of treatment based on the specific area and severity of the complaint.
treatments.aftercare: At each session, the doctor will provide the patient with detailed information regarding size of the needles, their placement, and the reasoning behind their usage and the duration of the session.

treatments.name: Cupping
treatments.summary: A suction-based therapy using cups placed on the skin to improve circulation and release muscular tension.
treatments.body: Cupping is a treatment method in which special cups are placed on the skin to create gentle suction. This stimulates circulation and helps release muscle tension. Within Traditional Chinese Medicine, cupping is also understood to support the body's broader recovery processes. At MC Balans, cupping is used as both a standalone treatment and in combination with other therapies where appropriate. Depending on your condition and treatment goals, our doctors determine whether cupping is the most suitable approach or whether it should be integrated into a broader treatment plan.
treatments.aftercare: During treatment, the doctor carefully places the cups on the affected areas to create controlled suction. The number of cups, their placement, and the treatment duration are adapted to the patient's individual condition and comfort.

treatments.name: Chinese Herbal Medicine
treatments.summary: An individually tailored herbal prescription, prepared to match each patient's specific symptoms and treatment goals.
treatments.body: Chinese Herbal Medicine is one of the oldest treatment methods within Traditional Chinese Medicine. Rather than relying on a standard prescription, herbal formulas are tailored to the individual patient, taking into account both the symptoms and the underlying pattern identified during the consultation. At MC Balans, every herbal prescription is prepared specifically for the patient. Chinese Herbal Medicine is often used alongside other treatments such as acupuncture and cupping to support recovery and, within the Traditional Chinese Medicine framework, to help restore the body's balance. As treatment progresses, prescriptions can be adjusted to reflect changes in the patient's condition.
treatments.aftercare: Patients receive a personalised herbal formula together with clear instructions on its preparation and use. During follow-up appointments, the doctor evaluates progress and adjusts the prescription where necessary to reflect changes in the patient's condition.

treatments.name: Nutrition & Movement
treatments.summary: Personalised nutrition and lifestyle guidance that supports recovery and helps prevent recurring complaints.
treatments.body: Nutrition and movement form the foundation of a healthy lifestyle and play an important role in both recovery and prevention. While other treatments focus on addressing existing complaints, healthy eating habits and regular physical activity help support the body's natural ability to maintain balance over the long term. At MC Balans, nutritional and lifestyle advice is integrated into treatment wherever appropriate. Recommendations are tailored to each patient's individual situation and complement other treatment methods, helping to support recovery while reducing the likelihood of recurring complaints.
treatments.aftercare: Patients receive practical advice tailored to their individual circumstances. Depending on the condition being treated, this may include recommendations regarding nutrition, movement, or other lifestyle adjustments that support the body's recovery alongside any medical or Traditional Chinese Medicine treatments.

treatments.name: PRP Therapy
treatments.summary: A Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) treatment used to support hair transplant aftercare and help with hair loss, drawing on the clinic's experience with hair transplantation and beauty treatments.
treatments.body: The doctors at MC Balans are trained in both Western and Eastern medicine, and their years of experience have made them competent in a wide range of treatments. This includes supporting hair transplantation and beauty clinics with aftercare, as well as offering PRP (Platelet Rich Plasma) treatments following hair transplantation. Many people who are not eligible for a hair transplant can also be well helped with PRP treatment, and our healthcare providers are specifically trained for this
treatments.aftercare: A small amount of blood is drawn and processed to separate the platelet-rich plasma. The PRP is then prepared and administered to the treatment area using a series of injections. The practitioner will guide you through the procedure and provide any relevant aftercare instructions.

treatments.name: Moxa Therapy
treatments.summary: A supplementary technique within Traditional Chinese Medicine that uses the heat of a burning moxa stick (made from mugwort herb) to stimulate acupuncture points.
treatments.body: Moxa therapy is a treatment method widely used within Traditional Chinese Medicine, typically used alongside acupuncture. It involves heating acupuncture points using a moxa stick — a cigar-shaped stick made from mugwort herb. During treatment, the stick is either held above the skin or used to warm the acupuncture needles themselves. The heat is thought to stimulate the flow of energy through the body.
treatments.aftercare: The practitioner heats the relevant acupuncture points using a moxa stick, either holding it above the skin or using it to warm the needles already in place, depending on the treatment plan.

treatments.name: Ear Acupuncture
treatments.summary: A specialization within acupuncture using very fine needles (or adhesive patches) placed on specific points of the outer ear.
treatments.body: Ear acupuncture is a specialization within acupuncture. A professional acupuncturist places very thin needles in the skin of the ear, stimulating the acupuncture points located there. Instead of needles, an ear seed can also be used for this purpose.
treatments.aftercare: During treatment, the acupuncturist identifies the relevant points on the outer ear and applies either thin needles or an ear seed, depending on the patient's situation and preference.
